title: Filter the ticket list by status
spec:
Let API clients list only the tickets in a given status.

GET /api/tickets accepts an optional `status` query parameter.
- `?status=<s>` returns only the workspace's tickets whose status is `<s>`, in the same order and with the same row shape as the unfiltered list. A valid status with no tickets returns `[]`.
- An unknown value (anything that is not one of todo, running, review, done, failed) is a 400 with `{ "error": ... }` whose message names the valid statuses.
- Without the parameter the endpoint behaves exactly as today (all tickets).

test/ticket-status-filter.test.ts is the locked acceptance test (read-only: do not edit or delete it). Make it pass without breaking any other test. Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Per-ticket test command
spec:
Let a ticket override the workspace test command for its own test gate. test/ticket-test-command.test.ts (read-only) defines the behavior; make it pass without breaking any other test.

- New migration server/migrations/008_ticket_test_command.sql: a nullable TEXT column test_command on tickets.
- server/app.ts: POST and PATCH /api/tickets accept an optional test_command: a string of at most 2000 chars, or null. "" and null store NULL; absent in a PATCH leaves it unchanged; any other type is a 400. Ticket reads already return it (t.*).
- server/runs.ts: the test gate runs the ticket's test_command when set, otherwise the workspace test_command. The test_result event's command and the failure reason use the command that actually ran.

Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Configurable turn budget for worker runs
spec:
Make the turn budget of worker runs a workspace setting instead of the hard-coded 50.

- New workspace setting `max_turns`: a whole number from 1 to 200, default 50. It needs a migration (the next number in server/migrations (009)).
- GET /api/settings returns it (50 when never set, also before a repository is saved). PUT /api/settings accepts a JSON integer or a numeric string (the settings form posts strings); omitted or "" means the default 50, like the other fields on that upsert. Anything else (0, 201, 2.5, "abc", null, true, arrays, ...) is a 400 whose message names max_turns, and a rejected save changes nothing.
- A worker run uses max_turns as its turn budget. A run that is still going after that many turns fails with a reason containing `turn budget exhausted (<n>)`; that is not a gate failure, so it is not retried.
- Planner runs (epic rounds) keep their own budget and must not be limited by max_turns. The CLI run path is unchanged.
- UI: add a number input for it to web/Settings.tsx (not covered by the test).

test/max-turns-setting.test.ts is the locked acceptance test (read-only: do not edit or delete it). Make it pass without breaking any other test. Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Ticket status webhooks
spec:
Notify an external system whenever a ticket's status changes.

Setting
- New workspace setting `webhook_url` (needs a migration; the next number in server/migrations (009)). Empty string = off, which is the default. GET /api/settings returns it; PUT /api/settings stores it (omitted = "", like the other fields on that upsert). A non-empty value must be an http: or https: URL of at most 2000 chars, otherwise 400 with an error message naming webhook_url.
- Add a URL input for it to web/Settings.tsx (not covered by the test).

Delivery
- Whenever a ticket's status actually changes (the new status differs from the old one), the server POSTs `Content-Type: application/json` to the workspace's webhook_url with the body
  `{ "event": "ticket.status", "ticket": { "id", "key", "title", "status", "previous_status" }, "at": "<ISO-8601 UTC timestamp>" }`
  where `key` is the ticket key as the API shows it (e.g. WH-3) and `title` / `status` are the values after the change.
- "Status change" means every way a ticket's status can change: a run being queued or finishing (including retries, failures and cancellation), approve, reject, auto-approve of children, a user PATCH /api/tickets/:id with a different status, and epic/planner rounds. Exactly one POST per change; none for creating a ticket, for edits that leave the status as it is (e.g. PATCH with the same status, or a title-only PATCH), or for a transition to the status the ticket already has.
- Delivery is fire-and-forget with a 5 second timeout and a single attempt (no retries). The request that caused the change (and the run pipeline) must never wait for it, and must never fail or change behaviour because of it: a dead, hanging or erroring URL leaves everything working.
- Every delivery attempt is recorded and readable at GET /api/webhook-deliveries (workspace-scoped, newest first, at most 100): an array of `{ id, ticket_id, url, ok, status_code, error, created_at }` where `ok` is a boolean (true for a 2xx answer), `status_code` the HTTP status or null when there was no answer, `error` null on success and a non-empty string otherwise (connection refused, timeout, non-2xx, ...). The row is written when the attempt finishes.

test/ticket-webhooks.test.ts is the locked acceptance test (read-only: do not edit or delete it). Make it pass without breaking any other test. Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Ticket labels
spec:
Add labels to tickets, end to end.

Data and API
- A label is a slug matching [a-z0-9-]{1,30}. Labels are normalized on input: trimmed, lowercased, deduplicated and sorted ascending (plain string comparison). A ticket has at most 10 labels, counted after normalization and dedup. Storage is up to you (needs a migration; the next number in server/migrations (009)).
- POST /api/tickets and PATCH /api/tickets/:id accept optional `labels`: an array of strings. Anything invalid (not an array, including null; a non-string element; an element that is not a valid slug after trimming/lowercasing; more than 10 labels) is a 400 whose message mentions labels, and a rejected request changes nothing. In a PATCH, `labels` replaces the whole set, `[]` clears it, and leaving it out keeps the current labels.
- Every ticket the API returns has `labels`, an array (`[]` when none): the list, GET /api/tickets/:id, POST/PATCH/approve/reject responses, and the children of an epic's detail view.
- GET /api/tickets?label=x returns only tickets carrying that label. The value is trimmed and lowercased like stored labels; an unknown or malformed value returns `[]` (200). Without the parameter the list is unchanged.
- GET /api/labels returns the workspace's labels as `[{ label, count }]`, sorted by label, where count is the number of the workspace's tickets carrying it; labels carried by no ticket are not listed. Counts must follow edits and ticket deletion, and never include other workspaces.

Planner
- The planner's create_ticket tool accepts optional `labels` (array of strings, same rules). The new child gets the epic's own labels plus the given ones (normalized, deduped, sorted), so labels flow down through sub-epics as well. Passing `[]` or nothing still inherits. Invalid labels, a non-array value, or more than 10 labels once inherited are a tool error (InvalidArguments mentioning labels) that creates no ticket.
- Keep the plannerTools(epic, outcome, since, queue) signature. The acceptance test passes an epic object with only the existing fields (id, workspace_id, key, title, spec, parent_id, provider_id, model), so the tool must look the epic's labels up itself. Also describe the new argument in the tool's input schema.

UI (not covered by the test)
- Board cards show the ticket's labels as chips, and the board has a label filter (any control you like).

test/ticket-labels.test.ts is the locked acceptance test (read-only: do not edit or delete it). Make it pass without breaking any other test. Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Personal API tokens
spec:
Let users call the API with personal access tokens instead of a browser session.

Token management (session only)
- POST /api/tokens `{ name, scope, expires_in_days? }`: name is 1-100 chars (trimmed); scope is exactly "read" or "write"; expires_in_days is a whole number 1-365, or absent/null for no expiry. Anything else is a 400. A user may hold at most 20 tokens per workspace (the 21st is a 409 whose message mentions 20; revoking one frees a slot). Returns 201 with `{ id, name, scope, created_at, last_used_at: null, expires_at, prefix, token }` where timestamps are unix milliseconds, `expires_at` = created_at + days*86400000 (or null), `token` is the secret and `prefix` its first 8 characters. The secret is `aht_` followed by at least 32 random URL-safe characters ([A-Za-z0-9_-]), and it is returned only by this response.
- Only a hash of the secret may be stored: the secret (or its random part) must not appear in any database row, nor in any later response. The acceptance test scans every table.
- GET /api/tokens lists the caller's own tokens in the active workspace, oldest first, as `{ id, name, scope, created_at, last_used_at, expires_at, prefix }` (exactly these keys, no secret). DELETE /api/tokens/:id revokes one of the caller's own tokens in the active workspace (204; anything else, including another user's or another workspace's token or an already revoked one, is a 404).
- These three routes need a session cookie. Called with a token (of any scope) they are a 403 whose message mentions tokens, so a token can never mint, list or revoke tokens.

Authenticating with a token
- Every /api route except /api/auth/* also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` as an alternative to the session cookie. The token acts as its user in the workspace it was created in. It does not follow later active-workspace switches of the user's sessions, and it stops working (401) if the user is no longer a member of that workspace.
- If an Authorization header is present it is used on its own: an unknown, malformed, non-Bearer, revoked or expired token is a 401, even when a valid session cookie is sent too. Expired tokens say "expired" in the error message. Expiry is judged by the server clock (Date.now()).
- A `read` token may only use GET (and HEAD). Any other method is a 403 whose error mentions the read scope, decided before routing and body validation (so also for unknown ids and invalid bodies), on every route: tickets, runs, approve/reject, settings, providers, lessons, prompts, evals, and so on. A `write` token may do whatever its user can, except manage tokens.
- The SSE endpoint GET /api/runs/:id/events works with a token like any other GET, with the same workspace isolation.
- `last_used_at` is set (ms) whenever a request authenticates with the token.
- Rate limit: a token may make 100 authenticated requests per minute (fixed one-minute windows are fine). The next one is a 429 with `Retry-After` (whole seconds, 1-60) and an error mentioning the rate limit, even if it would also be refused for its scope. Limits are per token: other tokens and session cookies are unaffected, and requests that fail authentication are not counted.

UI (not covered by the test): a section in the Settings page to create tokens (showing the secret once), list them, and revoke them. Document the feature in SPEC.md.

test/api-tokens.test.ts is the locked acceptance test (read-only: do not edit or delete it). Make it pass without breaking any other test. The next free migration number is 009. Run `npm test` before finishing.

title: Ticket comments, activity feed and live updates
spec:
Add comments and an activity feed to tickets, shown live, and let the agents read the comments.

Comments (/api/tickets/:id/comments)
- POST `{ body }` creates one (201); GET lists a ticket's comments oldest first; PATCH /:cid `{ body }` edits (200); DELETE /:cid deletes (204). Body must be a string of 1-10000 chars after trimming (stored trimmed); otherwise 400. Any member of the workspace may comment; only the author may edit or delete (403 for others). Unknown tickets/comments, a comment addressed through another ticket, and tickets of other workspaces are 404.
- A comment is `{ id, ticket_id, author_id, author_email, body, mentions, created_at, edited_at, deleted }` (exactly these keys; timestamps in unix ms, edited_at null until edited).
- Delete is soft: the comment stays in the list with body "[deleted]", `deleted: true` and `mentions: []`, its original text is no longer returned anywhere. Editing or deleting a deleted comment is a 404.
- Mentions: `@name` in the body names a workspace member by the local part of their email, case-insensitively. `mentions` is the sorted, deduplicated array of the lowercased local parts of the members named. Unknown names and users who are not in this workspace are ignored. The @ must not be preceded by a letter, digit, underscore or dot (so `bob@alice.dev` and `ping@bob` mention nobody); trailing `.`, `-` or `_` after the name are not part of it (`@bob.` is bob). Mentions are recomputed on edit.

Activity feed
- Items are `{ id, type, at, ticket_id, ticket_key, ... }`, `at` in unix ms, `id` a string unique within the workspace. Equal timestamps must keep the order things actually happened in. Types:
  - `comment`: `{ comment }` (the comment object above, in its current state), recorded when the comment is created. Edits and deletes add no item.
  - `status`: `{ from, to }`, recorded for EVERY real status change, however it happens: a run being queued or finishing (success, gate failure, cancellation), approve, reject, auto-approve of children, user PATCH, planner/epic rounds. Never for a transition to the same status (e.g. a retry that stays "running", PATCH with the current status) and never for creating a ticket.
  - `run`: `{ run_id, attempt, role, event: "started" | "finished", status, reason }` where `started` is recorded when the run actually begins executing (status null) and `finished` when it ends (status passed/failed/cancelled, reason as in run_finished, else null). A run cancelled while still queued only has a finished item. Eval-case runs are not part of a ticket's feed. Planner rounds are runs with role "planner".
  Within one run the order is: status todo>running, run started, run finished, then the resulting status change (e.g. running>review).
- GET /api/tickets/:id/activity returns the ticket's items oldest first (a plain array).
- GET /api/activity returns the workspace's items newest first as `{ items, next_cursor }`. Query parameters: `since` (ISO-8601 time; only items at or after it; unparsable is a 400), `limit` (whole number 1-100, default 50; anything else is 400), `cursor` (the opaque `next_cursor` of the previous page; invalid is a 400). `next_cursor` is null on the last page. Walking the pages must return every item exactly once even if new items arrive in between. Never shows other workspaces.
- GET /api/tickets/:id/activity/stream is a Server-Sent Events stream (text/event-stream): the response starts immediately with an SSE comment line (`: subscribed`) as soon as the stream is listening, and every item recorded after that is pushed as one `data:` event containing the same JSON as in the feed. No replay of older items, nothing from other tickets, 404 for other workspaces' tickets.

Agents see the comments
- The first message of every worker run and planner round gets a `# Comments` section placed before the ticket (before `# Task` / `# Epic`) when the ticket has non-deleted comments: the heading, a blank line, then one line per comment, oldest first, in the form `- <author_email>: <body>` (continuation lines of a multi-line body indented by two spaces), using the comment's current text. No section at all without comments. Eval-case runs (frozen) are unaffected.

UI (not covered by the test): a comment box and the feed on the ticket view, updating live. Document the feature in SPEC.md.
